subject: VPC GPU headroom & graceful fallback runbook
messages:
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Maria Garcia <maria.garcia@acme.com>
Cc: ops-archive@acme.com
Date: Thu, 3 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: VPC GPU headroom & graceful fallback runbook

Hi team — looping you in on a short runbook proposal for Acme's VPC private deployment. Goal: define clear throughput targets, warm-pool/headroom math, and a fallback path when the dedicated pool hits sustained saturation.

High-level asks from Acme (from last week's call): 1) sustain 1500 concurrent inference qps for 512-token median sequences, 2) <150ms P50 for the majority of requests, 3) automatic graceful degradation to a smaller model variant under sustained overload.

I've sketched an initial approach attached (vpc-headroom-runbook-v1.pdf) but need your ops + infra input on the following:
- What conservative headroom multiplier should we recommend for their 99th-percentile surges? (2x/3x?)
- Warm-pool sizing: how many prewarmed pods per shard to keep cold-starts <100ms?
- Network egress/ingress constraints in Acme's VPC and whether we should recommend an edge proxy/ingress sizing pattern.

Jonas — can you validate the capacity math assumptions on page 3 of the runbook? Naomi — can you call out any KV cache eviction / prefix-caching gotchas we've seen in similar on-prem jobs? Maria — if any of the asks above are off from your ops' expectations, flag and I'll update.

Proposed next step: 45-min sync today 3:30pm PT to align and ship the runbook.

— Dylan

--
Dylan Brooks
Director, Platform Solutions
Redwood Inference
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Maria Garcia <maria.garcia@acme.com>
Date: Thu, 3 Sep 2026 09:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: VPC GPU headroom & graceful fallback runbook

Thanks Dylan — quick notes after a pass through the PDF and our internal sim results (attached). Highlights:

- Headroom multiplier: for customer-facing low-latency workloads I recommend a conservative 2.5x on top of their sustained baseline. The baseline math in the doc assumes 1500 qps sustained -> provision for 3750 qps for headroom. That's where we keep warm-pool absorbency.
- Warm-pool sizing: on A100-equivalent nodes we typically keep 6 prewarmed pods per shard for 512-token medians to keep cold-start risk <1% under burst. That maps to ~12 pods per availability zone for 2 shard config in Acme's footprint.
- Eviction & prefix cache: two items — 1) ensure persistent prefix cache is pinned for top-traffic tenants or use conservative TTLs (30m) during business hours; 2) configure KV cache GC to prefer model-variant locality so warmups aren't cross-evicting between quantized and fp16 variants.
- Network: Acme's egress budget will be the gating factor. If their egress is limited to <2Gbps per AZ, we need to throttle outgoing large embedding responses and prefer chunked streaming for long outputs.

Operational fallback pattern (summary):
1) Fast failover to model-variant with 0.6x compute cost (lower precision) when 30s sustained queue length > threshold.
2) If egress threshold reached, switch to compressed response mode (truncate + fetch-on-demand links).
3) Canary: route 10% traffic to the fallback for 5 minutes before fully shifting.

I'll be on the 3:30pm call and will bring the sim CSV so we can tune numbers.

- Naomi

Naomi Feldman

From: Maria Garcia <maria.garcia@acme.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 3 Sep 2026 11:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: VPC GPU headroom & graceful fallback runbook

Thanks Dylan + Naomi — appreciate the level of detail. Quick clarifications from Acme infra:
- Our primary AZ has 3Gbps egress reserved for inference; secondary AZs are currently 1Gbps each.
- We can provision up to 40 A100-equivalent GPUs in the private pool for Q4, but prefer steady-state cost predictability.
- The fallback to lower-precision models is fine as long as we have a scoreboard for per-request quality degradation (we need an error-rate or hallucination metric threshold).

Can you include a short proc for how we measure quality drop during fallback and an ops-safe threshold? Also, what telemetry knobs should we expose in our console to make on-call decisions (key metrics)?

If possible, share a trimmed runbook that we can drop into our internal runbooks page.

— Maria
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
To: Maria Garcia <maria.garcia@acme.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 3 Sep 2026 15:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: VPC GPU headroom & graceful fallback runbook

Thanks Maria — good constraints, noted. Attached is a trimmed export of the runbook (vpc-headroom-runbook-v1.pdf) plus sim results we referenced (sim-results-20260902.csv). Summary of updates made based on Naomi's notes and Acme egress:
- Headroom: set to 2.5x baseline (provision target = 3750 qps). Given Acme's 40-GPU cap we'll map to a 3-shard layout with staggered warm pools to keep cost predictable while providing burst absorbency.
- Warm-pool: 6 prewarmed pods per shard in the primary AZ, 3 per shard in secondary AZs; warm-pool autoscaling policy keyed to 90th percentile short-window QPS.
- Fallback quality gating: add a per-candidate ROUGE-style scoring hook (or request-level acceptance rate) and a 6% degradation threshold for automatic fallback to compressed responses. Manual override retained for on-call.
- Telemetry to expose: per-model P50/P95 latency, queue length, per-tenant KV cache hit rate, egress rate per AZ, fallback-engaged boolean and degradation-score percentile.

Next steps: 1) Maria/Acme to confirm the 40-GPU commitment and AZ egress numbers in writing, 2) Ops playbook check: Naomi/Jonas to prepare a short runbook snippet for Acme's internal page by EOD tomorrow, 3) we ship the updated PDF and Jira INF-8894 will track follow-ups.

If that all looks good I'll lock the doc and send to Acme's runbook page.

— Dylan

Attachments: vpc-headroom-runbook-v1.pdf (runbook, 4 pages), sim-results-20260902.csv (summary of traffic sims)
